correctness.rationale: C PASS. Direct tube parametrization yields the exact Jacobian, principal curvatures and angular integral for |rκ|<1; fixed area/volume reduce to r and L. Supporting-line convexity of (1-z)^(-1/2) at q² gives both the global bound and its curvature-variance remainder, with equality only for constant positive κ, hence a circle. Support-function identity p=h+h'', exact second derivative F''(p)=r²(p²+2r²)/(p²-r²)^(5/2), vanishing first variation and Parseval prove the constrained sharp eigenvalue 9 and degree-two equality. Standalone quadrature checks were run; finite tests are auxiliary, not universal proof. Conditions reach>r prevent immersed/singular tubes.

value.rationale: V PASS. The geometry supplies two independent physical constraints (surface area and enclosed volume), fixing spine length and tube radius yet leaving an infinite-dimensional class of smooth planar cores. The theorem identifies the unique optimal shape and exact optimal energy at each feasible dimensionless aspect ratio, a positive quantitative curvature-variance gap, and a sharp mode-by-mode fixed-constraint local stability spectrum selecting second harmonics. This resolves a natural constrained shape-optimization problem, not an arbitrary polynomial slice or numerical increment; it does not claim novelty for established tube curvature formulas or general global Willmore inequality.
